followup_explanation:
This is a technical physics question — diffraction limits, transducer frequency, beam characteristics, and likely sources of experimental discrepancy. The routing decision comes down to raw capability on quantitative/scientific reasoning, since nothing about the content is sensitive or harm-adjacent.

Dunlin-235B has clearly stronger marks on the dimensions that matter here: MMLU-Pro (81.2 vs 75.4), GPQA Diamond (64.1 vs 55.6, a meaningful gap in graduate-level science reasoning), and Extraction & Retrieval (85.3 vs 78.5, relevant for pulling apart the theoretical-vs-measured comparison). Those differences are well outside run-to-run variance.

The task preferences didn't factor in much — this is warm, benign content, so Avocet's harm-aversion isn't triggered, and its generative appetite isn't really the relevant skill for a diagnostic physics problem. The friendly tone is the same either way. So the decision rests on capability, and Dunlin is the better fit.
